pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Rooms

Set high on Harrow Ridge at 1,640 metres, our five timber rooms look out across the Vell valley. Three rooms are open through November, while the remaining two reopen on 26 December.

Five rooms

→

Ridge Room

Sleeps 2 · 18 m²
Half board €210 a night

Hold this room

A double bed under the sloping eaves, with an east window that looks out over the cloud below. The room the keepers give first to anyone who wants the sunrise.

East window · Wool blankets · Washstand

→

Larch Room

Sleeps 2 · 16 m²
Half board €190 a night

Hold this room

Twin beds in larch-panelled walls, with a small desk for the evening. Quiet, warm from the stove below, and the easiest room to sleep in.

Twin beds · Small desk · Reading lamps

→

Bunk Loft

Six bunks · 30 m²
Half board €62 a bunk

Hold this room

Six timber bunks under the roof for walkers who share. Boots dry in the room below, and every bunk has its own lamp and a wool blanket.

Shared loft · Bunk lamps · Boot room below

→

Cairn Room

Reopens 26 Dec

Sleeps 4 · 26 m²
Half board €320 a night

Hold this room

A double bed and two singles for families, with room for luggage and a window that takes the morning sun. It reopens with the winter season on 26 December.

Double and two singles · Space for luggage · Morning light

→

Window Room

Reopens 26 Dec

Sleeps 1 · 11 m²
Half board €110 a night

Hold this room

A single bed and a desk set into a deep window, for one traveller who wants the cloud outside and a quiet evening in. It reopens on 26 December.

Single bed · Deep window desk · Reading lamp

What every room has

Every room at Kumoi Lodge is designed for warmth, rest, and quiet after hours on the path. Beds are dressed with fresh cotton sheets cared for by Sofia Marchetti, layered beneath pure wool blankets and heavy down duvets to keep the mountain chill at bay. Guests have access to hot water kettles, local herbal teas, washing basins, and personal reading lamps beside each bed. Downstairs, the heated boot room keeps footwear dry overnight. The lodge operates without television screens or digital distractions, allowing the soft murmur of the dining room stove and the stillness of the high ridge to shape the night.

  • Cotton sheets and wool blankets
  • Down duvets for the cold nights
  • A reading lamp at every bed
  • Kettle and local herbal teas
  • A washstand with hot water
  • Boot room with drying racks

Room by room

Ridge Room and Larch Room

The Ridge Room offers eighteen square metres under sloping eaves, featuring a double bed oriented toward the eastern window where morning light breaks above the clouds. At two hundred and ten euros a night for two guests, it includes full half board with evening supper and morning breakfast. The Larch Room spans sixteen square metres of solid larch panelling, fitted with twin beds and a small timber writing desk facing the quiet slopes. Available at one hundred and ninety euros a night for two guests, it also provides half board. Both rooms are open throughout November, heated by the central hearth and morning sun.

Bunk Loft, Cairn Room, and Window Room

The Bunk Loft covers thirty square metres, providing six sturdy timber bunks arranged for walkers traveling light along the ridge. Available at sixty-two euros per bunk including supper and breakfast, it remains open in November. Two additional spaces reopen on 26 December for the winter season: the Cairn Room and the Window Room. The Cairn Room measures twenty-six square metres with a double bed and two singles suited for families or groups of up to four guests at three hundred and twenty euros a night. The Window Room offers eleven square metres for a solo traveller, featuring a single bed and a desk set into a deep window at one hundred and ten euros a night.

Which rooms are open this month?

During November, Kumoi Lodge keeps three of its five rooms open: the Ridge Room, the Larch Room, and the six-bed Bunk Loft. This deliberate rhythm allows our small team to maintain the hearth, prepare fresh family-style suppers, and look after trail walkers before winter settles in fully. The Cairn Room and the solo Window Room remain closed for late autumn maintenance and will reopen on 26 December when our winter season begins. Guests hoping to stay during November can find open dates starting with our next free night on Friday 14 November.

See rates and booking

pages.title: The Stay
pages.content:
The Stay

Life at Kumoi Lodge follows the daylight and the rhythm of the cast-iron stove. We keep the house warm, gather around one table for supper, and bank the hearth as night settles over the ridge.

How a night is held

A stay at the ridge follows the natural rhythm of warmth, mountain light, and the banked fire. Rooms are ready with tea on the stove, the tub is lit on the open deck, supper is served at the long table, and by the end of the evening the lamps are turned low and the boots are drying on the racks.

  • Stove lit at 15:00
  • Boots dried overnight
  • Lamps low at 21:30
  • 15:00Rooms ready, tea on the stove
  • 16:30Tub fire lit
  • 18:30Supper at the long table
  • 21:30Stove banked, lamps low
  • 07:00Breakfast
  • 10:00Check-out (bags can stay till 14:00)

A night, in order

The rhythm of the day

A night on Harrow Ridge moves to a quiet, fixed schedule. Rooms are ready at 15:00, when a fresh kettle of tea is set atop the dining-room stove. At 16:30, Yusuf lights the cedar wood-fired outdoor tub out on the deck. Supper is served promptly at 18:30 at our single long table, bringing all guests together for a shared hot meal. By 21:30, the hearth fire is banked and lamps are turned low. Morning begins with Amara's breakfast at 07:00. Check-out is at 10:00, though walkers are welcome to leave packs in the boot room until 14:00.

Arriving and the evening

Guests arrive between 15:00 and 17:00, stepping in through the timber porch as the track closes to cars at dusk. Boots are exchanged for wool slippers in the drying room, coats hung on wooden pegs, and warm tea poured straight from the kettle. As mist pools in the valley, the outdoor wood-fired tub steams quietly on the open deck, available for forty-five minute private soaks at eighteen euros per room. At 18:30, Tomas Reyes-Bauer brings out a steaming pot of supper to the long table, where guests share bread, stories, and the warmth of the roaring stove.

Morning and leaving

Mornings begin early above the clouds. At 07:00, Amara Okoye sets out warm porridge, eggs, fresh butter, and bread baked before dawn in the kitchen oven. Lio Brandt stops by the long table with weather notes, checking ridge winds and trail safety for departing walkers. Check-out takes place by 10:00 so rooms can be aired and made ready for incoming travellers. Those spending a final day walking the nearby summits may leave heavy luggage in the drying room until 14:00 before beginning their journey back down to the valley.

The Bunk Loft at night

Six bunks, six lamps and boots drying in the room below: the loft for walkers who would rather share.

First snow at the cairn

A short walk from the door, the cairn marks the ridge. In the first snow it is the quietest place on the mountain.

What house rules keep the lodge restful?

To protect the peaceful atmosphere of Harrow Ridge, we ask all guests to observe a few simple guidelines. The house maintains quiet hours after 22:00, letting tired walkers sleep without disturbance. No vehicle traffic is permitted on the private track after dusk, when the gate is secured for safety. Dogs are welcome to sleep comfortably in the heated boot room, though they are not permitted in guest bedrooms or the dining hall. The drying room remains open all night so wet socks, boots, and jackets can dry thoroughly before the next morning's trek.

  • Quietafter 22:00
  • Carsnone on the track after dusk
  • Dogsboot room only
  • Drying roomopen all night

pages.title: The Table
pages.content:
The Table

Meals at Kumoi Lodge are hearty, unhurried, and served family-style at our single long timber table. We cook with mountain ingredients, bake daily bread, and welcome everyone to eat together after a day on the heights.

Supper

Served at 18:30
Tomas cooks, the table passes

Ask about diets

One pot, cooked by Tomas and passed along the long table, with bread from the morning bake. Vegetarian always; other needs with three days’ notice.

Tonight’s pot: Barley and lentil stew · Sourdough from the morning bake · Mountain cheese · Pickled beetroot · Baked apple

Breakfast

Served at 07:00
Amara’s bread, from the oven

Ask about diets

Porridge, eggs and Amara’s bread, set by the window with the cloud still below. A packed lunch for the trail is €12.

On the board: Porridge with honey · Soft eggs · Warm bread and butter · Preserves · Coffee and tea

Two meals a day

Supper at the long table

Every evening at 18:30, guests gather around the long timber table for supper prepared by co-keeper and cook Tomas Reyes-Bauer. Tomas prepares a single generous hot pot suited to cold mountain evenings, such as braised mountain roots, hearty stews, and savory broths served alongside thick slices of fresh sourdough. Food is passed by hand from guest to guest, fostering easy conversation among strangers. We always prepare a satisfying vegetarian alternative for every meal, and we gladly accommodate other dietary requirements provided guests notify us at least three days prior to their arrival.

Breakfast and morning bread

Before sunrise, Amara Okoye lights the bakery oven to knead and bake morning loaves for the entire lodge. Breakfast is served at 07:00 as dawn filters across the ridge and illuminates the sea of clouds below. The morning sideboard is laid with steaming oat porridge, soft-boiled eggs, fresh farmhouse butter, fruit preserves, and pots of strong hot coffee and mountain tea. Guests eat at their own pace by the deep window, watching the mist shift across the valley while fueling their bodies for long climbs ahead.

Packed lunch for the trail

Walkers heading out along the Harrow Ridge or crossing toward the Saddle can order a packed trail lunch for twelve euros. Prepared each morning by Amara and Tomas, each parcel contains a thick sandwich made on fresh hearth bread, a crisp mountain apple, hard cheese, and wholesome dried fruit or nuts. We also top up your thermos flasks with hot tea or boiling water before you set out from the boot room. Trail lunches should be requested at supper the evening before so they can be wrapped and ready at breakfast.

  • Bread, cheese, fruit
  • Flask filled at 07:30
  • Apple from the cellar

Packed lunch for the trail: €12

Ask about diets

Diets and allergies

Because we operate at 1,640 metres with provisions brought up the steep track, we cook a single communal supper each evening. A vegetarian option is always made available as part of our regular kitchen routine without requiring advance notice. For vegan meals, gluten-free bread, or specific food allergies, we ask guests to inform us at least three days in advance when booking their stay. This allows Tomas and Amara to source suitable mountain produce and prepare separate portions so every guest at the long table dines comfortably and safely.

Write to the desk

pages.title: Rates & Booking
pages.content:
Rates & Booking

All room rates at Kumoi Lodge include half board with evening supper at the long table and morning breakfast. We keep our booking terms straightforward and confirm every reservation directly within twenty-four hours.

Room rates and half board

Our nightly rates are simple, transparent, and built around half board. The Ridge Room is two hundred and ten euros for two guests. The larch-panelled Larch Room is one hundred and ninety euros for two guests. The spacious Cairn Room accommodates up to four guests for three hundred and twenty euros, while the solo Window Room is one hundred and ten euros. Individual bunks in the Bunk Loft are sixty-two euros per person. Half board includes supper and breakfast for each guest. Extras include our trail packed lunch at twelve euros and the outdoor wood-fired tub at eighteen euros per room for forty-five minutes.

Ridge Room

Sleeps 2 · 18 m²

Double bed under the eaves with the east window over the cloud, 18 m².

Half board €210 a night · Open in November

Larch Room

Sleeps 2 · 16 m²

Twin beds in larch panelling with a small desk, 16 m².

Half board €190 a night · Open in November

Bunk Loft

Six bunks · 30 m²

Six shared timber bunks for walkers, 30 m².

Half board €62 a bunk · Open in November

Cairn Room

Sleeps 4 · 26 m²

Double bed and two singles for families, 26 m².

Half board €320 a night · Reopens 26 Dec

Window Room

Sleeps 1 · 11 m²

Single bed with a desk at a deep window, 11 m².

Half board €110 a night · Reopens 26 Dec

Rates, half board

Half board is supper and breakfast. Prices are per night in euros.

Booking terms and seasons

Reservations require a thirty percent deposit upon confirmation, with the remaining balance settled at the lodge. We offer free cancellation up to fourteen days before your scheduled arrival date. Kumoi Lodge welcomes guests across two distinct mountain seasons: late spring through autumn from 1 May to 30 November, and winter from 26 December to 15 March. The lodge is closed for deep maintenance between 1 and 25 December, and again during the spring thaw from 16 March to 30 April. During November, three of our five rooms remain open, with our next free night falling on Friday 14 November.

  • Deposit30% to confirm
  • Confirmationby the keeper within 24 hours
  • Cancellationfree up to 14 days before arrival
  • Open seasons1 May – 30 Nov · 26 Dec – 15 Mar
  • Closed1–25 Dec · 16 Mar – 30 Apr

How to book

Booking a stay follows four straightforward steps without automated booking portals. First, select your preferred dates and room choice from our seasonal availability. Second, submit your reservation request via our online form or email us directly at stay@kumoilodge.example. Third, Clémence or Ines will personally review your request, confirm availability within twenty-four hours, and arrange your thirty percent deposit. Fourth, plan your journey to arrive at the ridge by 17:00. If snow or ice closes the upper track to vehicles, park at the gate car park at Vell Pass, and our keeper will meet you for a ten-minute drive up.

  • 1Choose dates and a room.
  • 2Send a request, by form or by email.
  • 3The keeper confirms within 24 hours and asks for the 30% deposit.
  • 4Arrive by 17:00. If the track is iced, leave the car at the gate car park and the keeper fetches you in ten minutes.

Every overnight stay at Kumoi Lodge is priced with half board included, beginning at sixty-two euros per night in the Bunk Loft. This covers your room or bunk, a warm evening supper cooked by Tomas Reyes-Bauer at the communal table, and Amara Okoye's hearty breakfast with freshly baked bread the next morning. Guests also enjoy unlimited hot tea from the dining-room stove, access to the heated boot and drying room, and local trail guidance from Lio Brandt. Only the forty-five-minute outdoor tub session and trail lunch parcels are billed as optional extras.

  • Choose dates
  • Send a request
  • Arrive by 17:00
Email a request

pages.title: Walks & Weather
pages.content:
Walks & Weather

Harrow Ridge stands at 1,640 metres above the Vell valley, offering immediate access to three established mountain trails. Walkers can explore high ridges, stone landmarks, and forest tracks in changing alpine weather.

Three trails from the lodge

Three marked routes leave directly from our timber doorstep. The Cairn Loop takes two hours and thirty minutes, covering 6.4 kilometres across gentle contours and rated easy. It winds past high pastures to the stone cairn before looping back along the eastern crest. The Ridge to the Saddle requires four hours, spanning eleven kilometres of exposed crest rated moderate, offering panoramic views when the valley below fills with cloud. The Old Track down to Vell is a 5-kilometre descent taking one hour and forty-five minutes, rated easy, following the historic herders' path down through larch groves to the valley road.

→

Cairn Loop

2 h 30 min · 6.4 km
Easy

Ask Lio about the weather

A gentle loop from the lodge door up to the stone cairn and back along the contour path, with the cloud usually below you.

→

Ridge to the Saddle

4 h · 11 km
Moderate

Ask Lio about the weather

Along the ridge crest to the Saddle and back. A longer day: ask the kitchen for the packed lunch (€12) and start after breakfast.

→

The Old Track down to Vell

1 h 45 min · 5 km
Easy, a descent

Ask Lio about the weather

The old herders’ track down through the larches to Vell. It only goes down, so check the bus times with the desk before you set out.

Reading the weather with Lio

Weather on Harrow Ridge changes quickly as moisture drifts up from the Vell valley. Most mornings begin above a vast sea of white cloud that blankets the lowlands, giving way to bright sun or sudden afternoon squalls. Lio Brandt monitors daily barometric pressure, wind speeds, and ridge conditions each morning, posting trail updates on the boot-room chalkboard. Before setting out on either the Cairn Loop or the Saddle trail, we encourage all guests to consult Lio about expected cloud cover, wind chill, and path ice, especially as winter approaches and first snow blankets the higher markers.

What to pack for ridge walking

Even on easy outings, high ridge conditions demand proper preparation. We advise every walker to carry six essential items on the trails: sturdy broken-in walking boots with deep tread, a windproof and waterproof outer shell jacket, an insulating wool or fleece mid-layer, a detailed paper map and magnetic compass, a refillable water flask, and a reliable headlamp with spare batteries. Sudden temperature drops are common at 1,640 metres. Having the right layers ensures that whether you walk two hours or four, you remain comfortable, dry, and safe until you return to the warm stove.

  • Waterproof shell
  • Warm layer and hat
  • Sturdy boots
  • Water and the packed lunch
  • A map and Lio’s weather note
  • Head torch for the late descent

Sudden storms

When walking above the cloud line, weather can shift from calm sunlight to dense mountain mist in under an hour. If visibility drops on the exposed Ridge to the Saddle, walkers should pause, check trail cairns, and turn back toward the lodge before winds rise. Lio Brandt is always on hand at breakfast to discuss route choices, wind forecasts, and return timings. We ask all guests to log their intended route on the boot-room board and aim to return well before dusk at 17:00, when daylight fades and temperatures drop sharply.

Ask Lio about the weather

pages.title: Getting here
pages.content:
Getting here

Kumoi Lodge sits on Harrow Ridge at 1,640 metres, reached by a gravel mountain track above the Vell valley. Whether arriving by road or rail, please plan your ascent to reach us before dusk.

Getting here

Drive to the gate car park at Vell Pass at 1,420 metres, where the 2.2 kilometre mountain track begins. Guests can walk the remaining 35 minutes up through the larches, or call for the keeper to meet them in ten minutes if the track is iced.

  • Gate car park, 1,420 m
  • 35 minutes on foot
  • Call for a pick-up

By public transport: train to Vell station, then bus 4 to the Pass, three a day.

The way up

Arriving by car and mountain track

To reach Kumoi Lodge by road, navigate toward Vell Pass, where our private gate car park is situated at 1,420 metres. From this gate, a gravel track winds 2.2 kilometres up the ridge to the lodge at 1,640 metres. Walking this scenic section takes approximately thirty-five minutes on foot. If the track is iced, or if you carry heavy bags, park at the gate and phone us; our keeper will arrive in our four-wheel-drive vehicle to fetch you in ten minutes. Because the private track closes to vehicles at dusk, all guests must arrive at the lodge by 17:00.

Public transport and train connections

Travelling by public transport is straightforward with advance planning. Take the railway to Vell station in the valley, which connects regularly with regional rail lines. From outside Vell station, take bus 4 directly up to the stop at Vell Pass; this bus runs three times a day throughout our open seasons. From the bus stop at the Pass gate, you can either walk the 2.2-kilometre gravel track up to Harrow Ridge or contact the lodge desk between 08:00 and 20:00 to coordinate a keeper pick-up from the gate car park.

Lodge hours and check-in times

Our daily lodge hours ensure smooth arrivals and restful evenings. Guest rooms are fully aired, warmed, and ready by 15:00. We ask all guests to arrive by 17:00, as the private access track is locked at dusk for mountain safety. Morning check-out is completed by 10:00, though departing guests are welcome to store luggage in the heated drying room until 14:00 while exploring the nearby trails. Our telephone and reception desk remain open daily from 08:00 to 20:00 to assist with directions, arrival updates, and transport arrangements.

  • Rooms ready15:00
  • Arrive by17:00
  • Check-out10:00
  • Desk08:00–20:00

When the track is iced

During late autumn and winter conditions, ice and snow frequently settle on the upper bends of Harrow Ridge Track 4. When ice signs are posted at the Vell Pass entrance, guests driving private cars should not attempt the steep ascent. Instead, leave your vehicle at the secure gate car park at 1,420 metres and telephone the desk at +00 41 555 0164. Our keeper will drive down in the lodge vehicle equipped with chains to collect you and your luggage, bringing you up to the warmth of the hearth in ten minutes.

Write to the desk

pages.title: Keepers
pages.content:
Keepers

Kumoi Lodge is looked after by seven people who live and work together on Harrow Ridge. We keep the fires stoked, bake daily loaves, and maintain a warm shelter high above the weather.

History of the ridge lodge

The stone foundation of Kumoi Lodge was laid in 1931, originally built as a humble timber hut for local herders tending high summer pastures on Harrow Ridge. In 1964, the structure was expanded and officially opened as a mountain lodge to welcome walkers traversing the heights above the Vell valley. The present keepers took over stewardship in 2009, carefully restoring the larch timbers, preserving the herders' hearth, and maintaining the house as an intimate, quiet refuge. Over ninety years since its initial construction, the lodge continues to offer simple shelter, hot suppers, and honest hospitality.

Our approach to mountain hospitality rests on a single guiding principle: come in out of the weather; the stove is already lit. Living above the cloud line demands patience, practical care, and respect for changing mountain seasons. Rather than expanding our footprint, we deliberately keep just five rooms and gather everyone around one long table each evening. There are no televisions, no rushed schedules, and no commercial distractions here. We believe that warmth, dry wool, a steaming bowl of broth, and good company are the true luxuries of a life spent in high country.

Ines keeps the stove

Ines Halvorsen has kept the lodge since 2009. She splits the kindling, lights the stove and knows when the weather will turn.

The tub, lit at 16:30

Yusuf lights the wood-fired tub on the timber deck, forty-five minutes per room for €18, with the cloud settling below you.

The keeping team

Seven people share the daily work of keeping the lodge running smoothly at 1,640 metres. Ines Halvorsen has served as head keeper since 2009, overseeing the house and welcoming guests. Tomas Reyes-Bauer works as co-keeper and cooks our evening suppers at the long table. Amara Okoye manages morning baking, preparing daily sourdough and breakfast porridge. Lio Brandt monitors track safety, local weather patterns, and mountain walks. Yusuf Demir cuts wood, banks the cast-iron stoves, and manages maintenance. Clémence Aubry handles reservations and the desk, while Sofia Marchetti looks after guest rooms, blankets, and fresh linen.

Ines Halvorsen

Keeper since 2009

Ines runs the house and the stove. She decides when the supper bell rings and when the track is closed to cars.

Tomas Reyes-Bauer

Co-keeper and supper cook

Tomas cooks the one pot at 18:30 and plans the table around what the track brings up. Vegetarian comes first, and the rest follows.

Amara Okoye

Bread and breakfast

Amara is up before dawn to knead the day’s loaves. Her porridge, eggs and warm bread are on the board at 07:00.

Lio Brandt

Track, weather and walks

Lio walks the upper track each morning and writes the weather note for the board. Ask him before you choose a route.

Yusuf Demir

Wood, stove and repairs

Yusuf splits and stacks the larch, lights the tub at 16:30 and banks the stove at 21:30. He mends whatever the winter has loosened.

Clémence Aubry

Bookings and the desk

Clémence answers the desk from 08:00 to 20:00 and keeps the calendar. Write to her for dates, diets and arrival times.

Sofia Marchetti

Rooms and linen

Sofia makes the beds, airs the rooms and keeps the wool blankets in the linen press. She leaves hot water at every washstand.

Who looks after the daily running of the lodge?

The daily operation of Kumoi Lodge is managed on-site by our resident team rather than remote operators. Keepers Ines Halvorsen and Tomas Reyes-Bauer live on the ridge year-round, tending the house alongside Yusuf Demir, Amara Okoye, Lio Brandt, Sofia Marchetti, and Clémence Aubry. From lighting the outdoor cedar tub and baking morning loaves to checking snow markers and laundering linens, every task is carried out directly by the people who greet you at the door. When you arrive, you are welcomed into a working home where every keeper takes pride in mountain stewardship.

“Come in out of the weather; the stove is already lit.”

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

Get in touch with the keepers of Kumoi Lodge for availability, route questions, or booking inquiries. We answer every message personally from our desk on Harrow Ridge.

Write or call

The reception desk at Kumoi Lodge is attended daily from 08:00 to 20:00 by Clémence Aubry and Ines Halvorsen. You can telephone us directly at +00 41 555 0164 during desk hours to discuss upcoming availability, weather conditions, or travel arrangements. For general inquiries and reservation requests, please email stay@kumoilodge.example; we respond to all messages within twenty-four hours. Our postal address is Kumoi Lodge, Harrow Ridge Track 4, 8742 Vell. Because we are situated in a quiet mountain setting, we do not operate automated phone menus, ensuring you always speak directly with a resident keeper.

  • stay@kumoilodge.example
  • +00 41 555 0164
  • Desk 08:00–20:00
  • Emailstay@kumoilodge.example
  • Phone+00 41 555 0164
  • Desk08:00–20:00
  • PostHarrow Ridge Track 4, 8742 Vell

Operating seasons and schedule

Kumoi Lodge welcomes guests during two distinct mountain periods: our summer and autumn season from 1 May to 30 November, and our winter season from 26 December to 15 March. The lodge remains completely closed between 1 and 25 December for maintenance and woodcutting, and again between 16 March and 30 April during spring runoff. When visiting during open months, guest rooms are ready at 15:00 and all arrivals must be completed by 17:00 before the gate track closes at dusk. Morning check-out is at 10:00, with luggage storage available until 14:00.

Rates and current availability

Half board pricing starts at sixty-two euros per night for a single bunk in the Bunk Loft, one hundred and ten euros for the single Window Room, one hundred and ninety euros for the Larch Room, two hundred and ten euros for the Ridge Room, and three hundred and twenty euros for the family Cairn Room. During November, three of our five rooms are open for reservations, with our next free night occurring on Friday 14 November. The Cairn and Window rooms reopen on 26 December. All bookings include full supper and breakfast at our communal table.

See rates and booking

Urgent arrival news

If you encounter unexpected delays on the road from Vell or miss a connecting bus at Vell station, please call our desk promptly at +00 41 555 0164. Because the private gravel track past the gate car park at 1,420 metres closes to vehicular traffic at dusk, knowing your estimated arrival time allows keeper Yusuf Demir or Lio Brandt to coordinate a pick-up. Calling before 17:00 ensures we can meet your vehicle at the lower car park and transport your bags before supper is served at 18:30.

Call the desk

posts.title: The night the track closed
posts.excerpt: When an unexpected November blizzard buried Harrow Ridge and sealed the track down to Vell, twelve stranded guests gathered around one hot pot and the glowing hearth.
posts.content:
By three in the afternoon, the cloud sea that normally rests deep in the Vell valley had begun to climb the eastern flanks of Harrow Ridge. At 1,640 metres, the air turned sharply cold, and what had begun as a light flurrying mist transformed within an hour into heavy, horizontal snow. Lio Brandt came in through the boot-room door, stamping white crust from his wool trousers, to confirm what everyone had begun to suspect: the upper two kilometres of Harrow Ridge Track 4 were drifting rapidly shut, and no vehicle would be descending the mountain until morning.

By 17:00, dusk had fallen completely over the pass, and the lower gate at 1,420 metres was secured for the night. Inside the lodge, twelve people took off their outer coats and hung them along the wooden pegs in the hall. There were two guests staying in the Ridge Room, two in the Larch Room, six walkers sharing the timber bunks in the Bunk Loft, and two hikers who had cut their descent from the Saddle short when the blizzard hit. Outside, the wind rattled the window frames, but inside, Yusuf Demir was already stacking dry larch logs into the dining-room stove, coaxing a steady amber blaze from the embers.

In the kitchen, co-keeper Tomas Reyes-Bauer took stock of the evening supper. With twelve hungry mouths and no chance of resupply, there was no complex menu to consider, only the simple necessity of one honest pot. Tomas pulled root vegetables, leeks, and dried white beans from the cold store beneath the pantry, setting a broad cast-iron cauldron directly over the stove heat. Into it went cured pork, smoked bacon, chopped cabbage, and handfuls of dried thyme gathered from the ridge during summer. As the broth began to bubble and steam rose toward the heavy ceiling beams, the savory aroma spread into every corner of the house.

Amara Okoye emerged from the kitchen carrying thick wooden cutting boards piled high with sourdough loaves baked earlier that morning, while Ines Halvorsen lit beeswax candles down the centre of the long table. Clémence Aubry helped pour mugs of steaming herbal tea, and Sofia Marchetti brought down extra wool blankets from the linen press for anyone still feeling the drafts. At 18:30 precisely, Tomas carried the heavy pot to the middle of the table on a trivet. Bowls were passed from hand to hand, strangers poured soup for their neighbours, and crusts of dark bread were torn and dipped into the rich, steaming stew.

Any initial anxiety about blocked roads and missing schedules dissolved under the steady warmth of the hearth. For three hours, the dining room hummed with laughter, route discussions, and mountain stories shared across the timber boards. Outside, snow continued to pile against the shutters, sealing Harrow Ridge in white stillness. At 21:30, Yusuf stoked the embers one last time and banked the iron stove for the night. The lamps were turned low, and twelve well-fed travellers made their way up the wooden stairs to sleep under heavy down duvets. The mountain track was closed, but the house had done exactly what it was built to do: welcome those caught in the weather, set a pot on the fire, and keep the night safe.
